sources.title: closefrom(3) child cleanup policy
sources.sections_read: DESCRIPTION, RETURN VALUES, ERRORS, dated footer.
sources.confirmed: closefrom(fd) removes all descriptors numbered fd and above. The archived manual is dated May 31, 2007 and identifies OpenBSD 5.2.
sources.limits: It is a platform-specific API and closes deliberately shared extra descriptors too; every relevant launch path must adopt the policy or arrange explicit exceptions. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.

sources.title: FD_CLOEXEC per-descriptor inheritance control
sources.sections_read: DESCRIPTION on fork, execve, and F_SETFD; dated footer.
sources.confirmed: The archived manual explains inherited descriptors after fork and FD_CLOEXEC closing a descriptor on successful execve, with clearing the bit restoring inheritance.
sources.limits: It acts on exec, not fork alone; descriptors created without the flag by external code remain exposed, and setting the flag after creation leaves a concurrency gap. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: pre_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.

sources.title: O_CLOEXEC on open/openat
sources.sections_read: Flag definitions, descriptor defaults, standards, dated footer.
sources.confirmed: The archived manual defines O_CLOEXEC to set FD_CLOEXEC on the new descriptor and lists ordinary open/openat behavior.
sources.limits: Platform support and fallback behavior must be checked; a separate open-then-fcntl sequence can race with another thread's fork and exec, as the retrieved Linux manual explains. sources.version_or_date: live Linux man-pages; post-2013 POSIX.1-2024 material
sources.sections_read: pipe2 signature, O_CLOEXEC description, history and standards.
sources.confirmed: pipe2 accepts O_CLOEXEC to mark both pipe ends at creation; the page records Linux 2.6.27/glibc 2.9 history and contains current POSIX.1-2024 material.

sources.title: dup3(..., O_CLOEXEC)
sources.sections_read: dup/dup2 flags, dup3 O_CLOEXEC, error and history sections, colophon.
sources.confirmed: dup and ordinary dup2 produce a duplicate without FD_CLOEXEC, whereas dup3 accepts O_CLOEXEC. The page describes atomic replacement and the oldfd==newfd difference.
sources.limits: Ordinary dup/dup2 clear close-on-exec on a new duplicate, which can be useful for intentional child redirection; dup3 rejects identical old and new descriptor numbers, unlike dup2. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.

sources.title: GLib spawn descriptor and standard-stream flags
sources.sections_read: G_SPAWN_LEAVE_DESCRIPTORS_OPEN, standard stream flags, CLOEXEC_PIPES, version header.
sources.confirmed: Without LEAVE_DESCRIPTORS_OPEN, GLib closes descriptors other than standard streams before exec; standard input has a separate inheritance option. Current docs also list pipe CLOEXEC and newer standard-stream flags.
sources.limits: This protects only launches routed through GLib and therefore cannot cover all launch paths or external modules by itself; the current flag set includes later additions. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.

sources.title: socket(..., SOCK_CLOEXEC, ...)
sources.version_or_date: live Linux manual; specific publication date not established in displayed excerpt
sources.sections_read: DESCRIPTION and type flags, including SOCK_CLOEXEC.
sources.confirmed: The socket type argument accepts SOCK_CLOEXEC to set FD_CLOEXEC when creating the descriptor; this is a constructor-level mechanism rather than a spawn-wrapper-only policy.
sources.limits: This constructor does not by itself audit other descriptor-producing networking operations, and support must be checked per platform. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.

sources.title: POSIX spawn file actions
sources.sections_read: PROLOG; file_actions/FD_CLOEXEC ordering and descriptor 0/1/2 behavior in DESCRIPTION.
sources.confirmed: POSIX spawn first applies ordered file actions and then closes descriptors carrying FD_CLOEXEC. The standard separately discusses descriptors 0, 1 and 2, and otherwise permits open parent descriptors to survive.
sources.limits: The interface does not automatically discard every unmarked descriptor and covers only callers that use the spawn path; it complements a descriptor-creation policy. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: post_decision. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.

sources.title: open.2.html
sources.version_or_date: live Linux manual; specific publication date not established in displayed excerpt
sources.sections_read: DESCRIPTION, default inheritable flag, O_CLOEXEC concurrency discussion.
sources.confirmed: The manual explains that setting FD_CLOEXEC in a separate fcntl call races with a concurrent fork plus exec and that O_CLOEXEC avoids that gap at descriptor creation.
sources.limits: This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.

sources.title: Go ForkLock and explicit retained-descriptor policy
sources.version_or_date: live source; 2009 copyright does not date the retrieved revision
sources.sections_read: ForkLock design comments, per-constructor rules, CloseOnExec implementation, ProcAttr.Files, forkExec call path.
sources.confirmed: Go's public source combines close-on-exec defaults and explicit retained descriptors with a reader/writer lock around fallback descriptor creation and fork. It prefers atomic OS operations and explicitly notes that potentially blocking opens cannot always hold the lock, leaving a race on fallback paths.
sources.limits: All participating descriptor creators and launchers must honor the lock; external native code can bypass it, and the source explicitly leaves a race for potentially blocking open fallbacks. This is the recorded read scope, not a full-document or deployment validation. Evidence time class: unknown. Original read and any failures remain in runs/A/C11.json.
